paths.description: Public gateway entry page, the site’s only visible content template and outbound-action journey. Covered desktop/mobile, preference media, keyboard/focus, no-JS, performance, network, security and memory conditions. External platoboost.app destinations were excluded because they are different-site surfaces outside this host audit.
Representative unknown-route/error state at /does-not-exist to assess system-state clarity and recovery. No authenticated/account flow exists on the rendered host, so none could be covered.

findings.summary: The gateway forces one dark palette instead of following the user’s color-scheme preference.
findings.evidence: Default and prefers-color-scheme: dark screenshots are byte-identical; the DOM probe reports color-scheme: normal and no prefers-color-scheme rule.
findings.suggestedFix: Declare color-scheme: light dark and define preference-driven light and dark surface/text tokens with prefers-color-scheme or light-dark().

findings.summary: The first-view copy weakens clarity and credibility.
findings.evidence: Desktop/mobile screenshots show an unexplained “Gateway”, mixed Plato/Platoboost naming, and the typo “check out or website”.
findings.suggestedFix: Use one product name, explain why the user landed on this gateway, and correct the copy to “check out our website”.

findings.summary: The not-found state does not provide a recovery action.
findings.evidence: The /does-not-exist probe and screenshot show “An error occured”, technical detail/copy affordance, and legal links, but no retry, home, back, or primary destination.
findings.suggestedFix: Give the state a clear 404 title, plain-language explanation, and prominent Home/Back/Retry actions while preserving context.

findings.summary: The tiny gateway paints too slowly under Lighthouse mobile conditions.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse measured FCP and LCP at 3.6 s (performance 0.82), outside the good LCP threshold; the less-throttled trace measured 1.43 s and no blocking, so network/resource delivery is the main risk.
findings.suggestedFix: Server-render the first viewport and remove non-critical JavaScript from the critical path; keep the LCP text in initial HTML.

findings.summary: Critical delivery is oversized and hashed assets have short cache lifetimes.
findings.evidence: HAR records 729,513 transferred bytes for six requests, including 554,908 bytes of first-party JS; Lighthouse estimates 411 KiB repeat-visit savings from longer caching. The module script is deferred by type=module, while the 5.8 KiB stylesheet is genuinely render blocking.
findings.suggestedFix: Ship initial HTML, split the gateway bundle, and give content-hashed JS/CSS long immutable cache lifetimes.

findings.summary: Most JavaScript shipped to this simple page is unused.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse reports 504 KiB potential savings: 448,564 bytes unused in the first-party bundle (80.9%) and 67,808 bytes unused in gtag.
findings.suggestedFix: Create a gateway-specific entry bundle, tree-shake unused application code, and defer/load analytics only after an appropriate consent and need decision.

findings.summary: The document has an illogical heading and landmark structure.
findings.evidence: The DOM/probe shows two nested <main> elements, no H1, an empty H3 for the icon, and the visible title as another H3.
findings.suggestedFix: Use one <main>, make “Welcome to the Gateway” the H1, and mark the decorative icon aria-hidden rather than representing it as an empty heading.

findings.summary: The large first-party JavaScript bundle has no valid source map.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse best-practices diagnostics report “Large JavaScript file is missing a source map” for index-d2eb3afb.js.
findings.suggestedFix: Generate and deploy a matching production source map, or intentionally upload it to the error-monitoring service while configuring deployment diagnostics accordingly.

findings.summary: The page lacks a meta description and its title is only a brand name.
findings.evidence: DOM and Lighthouse show title “Platoboost” and no meta[name=description]; Lighthouse SEO score is 0.82.
findings.suggestedFix: Use a descriptive title such as “Platoboost creator monetization gateway” and add a concise description matching visible content.

findings.summary: Core content and primary destinations disappear for non-JavaScript crawlers.
findings.evidence: Discoverability reports 0% rendered-word coverage and a blank crawler screenshot. Primary actions are <button> elements with no href, while only legal links are crawlable anchors.
findings.suggestedFix: Render the gateway content in server HTML and implement destination actions as descriptive <a href> links, enhancing them with JavaScript only when needed.

findings.summary: Indexing signals are incomplete and robots/sitemap endpoints serve the app shell.
findings.evidence: The page has no canonical URL; /robots.txt and /sitemap.xml both return status 200 with the 478-byte HTML shell. Lighthouse reports 14 robots.txt syntax errors.
findings.suggestedFix: Serve valid text/plain robots.txt and XML sitemap responses, add a self-referencing canonical, and align indexing policy with this public gateway.

findings.summary: The gateway has no social preview or structured entity metadata.
findings.evidence: DOM inspection found no canonical/description and no Open Graph, Twitter Card, or JSON-LD metadata despite presenting a product/organization gateway.
findings.suggestedFix: Add accurate Open Graph/Twitter metadata and minimal Organization or SoftwareApplication JSON-LD that matches the visible page.

findings.summary: Transport is HTTPS, but baseline XSS/header protection and cookie flags are missing.
findings.evidence: Headers evidence reports no CSP, HSTS, or X-Content-Type-Options. Both _ga cookies are not Secure, use SameSite=None, and persist for 400 days.
findings.suggestedFix: Add HSTS, a restrictive nonce/hash-based CSP, nosniff, and set analytics cookies Secure with an appropriate SameSite policy and shorter retention.

findings.summary: Google tracking runs immediately on a one-screen gateway.
findings.evidence: Tracker/HAR evidence shows Google Tag Manager and Google Analytics on load, 166,677 third-party bytes, an immediate page_view, and two 400-day analytics cookies.
findings.suggestedFix: Decide whether analytics is necessary here; if retained, load a minimal privacy-preserving setup after valid consent, minimise fields/retention, and batch events.

findings.summary: Browser-enforced framing, referrer, and permission defenses are absent.
findings.evidence: Headers evidence reports no frame-ancestors/X-Frame-Options, Referrer-Policy, or Permissions-Policy in addition to the missing CSP/HSTS.
findings.suggestedFix: Set CSP frame-ancestors, Referrer-Policy, and a least-privilege Permissions-Policy; use X-Frame-Options as a legacy fallback where appropriate.

findings.summary: The gateway is a client-rendered shell with no usable no-JavaScript fallback.
findings.evidence: The raw response is 478 bytes with only one content token; discoverability reports 0% content coverage and the crawler/no-JS screenshot is blank, while the rendered page contains 214 text characters.
findings.suggestedFix: Server-render or statically emit the heading, explanation, destination links, and legal links; layer client behavior on top.

findings.summary: Unknown routes render a generic error without useful recovery.
findings.evidence: The tested /does-not-exist route renders “An error occured” and no retry/home/back action; it also appears within the same client shell.
findings.suggestedFix: Return an intentional HTTP 404 page with a clear message, recovery links, and a server-rendered fallback.

findings.summary: The resource footprint is disproportionate to 22 rendered content tokens.
findings.evidence: HAR transfers 729,513 bytes and Lighthouse identifies 504 KiB of unused JavaScript for a 32-element, one-card page.
findings.suggestedFix: Replace the shared application bundle with static HTML/CSS and a tiny optional module for only the interactions this gateway needs.

findings.summary: Analytics accounts for a large share of page weight without visible user value.
findings.evidence: Google Tag Manager transfers 166,677 bytes, about 23% of the 729,513-byte load, and triggers Analytics on this simple gateway.
findings.suggestedFix: Remove analytics from the gateway or defer a smaller privacy-preserving measurement path until needed and consented.
